Four photographic examples are paired with descriptions: (1) Community-based, participatory, and Indigenous and local knowledge methods, tools, and protocols (e.g., journals, printed survey forms, community maps) facilitate engagement of diverse audiences. (2) Ictio.org is an application and open and safe database to collect and share information on Amazonian migratory fish. (3) Data is safely transferred and stored in servers; open data is then accessible to multiple audiences with diverse levels of access and in user-friendly formats. (4) Collaboration is enabled through carefully designed methodologies, in-person and virtual meetings, social media, Google platform and tools. The four photos show a group gathered outdoors, hands using a phone among fish, people seated around displayed materials, and a large group gathered outside a building.
